what: User thinking bigger: aide-memory as FOUNDATION for something larger, not the end product. Potential pivots: (1) memory for ALL AI workflows not just coding (regular Claude, Cowork, other tools), (2) cloud-hosted version for everyday people, (3) conversation context embeddings, (4) connect to non-coding tools. Binary distribution enables better pro gating since users can't override code. Key concern: everyone releasing free tools — need clever monetization beyond $10/user/month subscription. Need to figure out what the BIGGER product is that memory enables. The foundation should be protected (binary) so what's built on top isn't easily replicated.
why: Major strategic pivot consideration. User sees aide-memory not as the product but as infrastructure for something bigger — possibly a cloud-hosted AI context layer that works across ALL tools (not just coding agents). This fundamentally changes the product vision if pursued.
